summary: The final part of Parkevtate Vosianc's five-part Nike deep dive delivers his verdict on September 22: Nike remains a buy, reiterated at $36.35 after his initial upgrade at $40 around August 19. The latest quarter was unvarnished: overall sales fell 1% YoY, modest North America growth was more than offset by rapidly declining Greater China sales; Nike Direct was down 9%, Nike Digital down 12%, stores down 7% — while wholesale revenue grew 1%, early evidence that CEO Elliott Hill's wholesaler-relationship rebuild is bearing fruit. Gross margin of 49.2% was flattered by a 900-basis-point tariff refund; excluding it, gross margin was 40.2%, down 10bps — meaning this is an organic demand decline (falling sales AND falling margins), driven by macro pressure on disposable income and rising competition, not by deliberate price discipline. He credits management for keeping inventory flat into a demand decline, and wants it down low-single-digits in coming quarters. His broader macro view: consumers are depleting savings and maxing credit cards, with non-substitutable essentials (rent, healthcare) crowding out discretionary buys like sneakers — hurting Nike, Adidas, On and Lululemon alike. He warned Nike was too expensive at $175, $100, $75 and $50, only upgrading at $40. At a forward P/E of 16 — the cheapest in many years and near the $36.18 52-week low — he sees a dollar-cost-averaging entry, though his DCF fair value of $31 means it's slightly overvalued on DCF and undervalued on P/E (slightly undervalued overall). Calls per supplied list: NKE BUY @ $36.35.
